events.title: Leo XIII promulgates Rerum Novarum
events.shortBlurb: The encyclical on capital and labor laid the foundation of modern Catholic social teaching…
body: On 15 May 1891 Leo XIII, pope since 1878, published the encyclical Rerum Novarum, 'Of New Things,' on the condition of the working classes. It mourned that the industrial age had left laborers 'surrendered, isolated and helpless, to the hardheartedness of employers and the greed of unchecked competition.'

Against the socialists it defended the right of private property as founded in nature; against unbridled capitalism it taught that labor is no mere commodity, that the worker is owed a wage sufficient to support himself and his family, that the state must protect the poor, and that working men may lawfully band together in associations of their own.

Leo, born Vincenzo Pecci in 1810, was eighty-one when the letter appeared. It became the charter of modern Catholic social teaching, and later popes have kept its anniversaries: Pius XI with Quadragesimo Anno in 1931, John XXIII with Mater et Magistra in 1961, and John Paul II with Centesimus Annus in 1991.
